messages:
jia: ran a small microbench on the multilanguage holdout (en/es/zh) with int6 quant and baseline fp16 this morning. weird drop at recall@10 for zh. attaching quick outputs.
jia: command I used:
```
./run_microbench --model=heron-int6 --dataset=multi_holdout_2k --k=10 --lang=zh,en,es --embed-batch=512
```

matt: can you paste the table? small threads are easier to triage :slightly_smiling_face:

jia: pasted below (precision/recall@k). numbers are averaged over 3 runs.
```
model        lang  recall@1  recall@5  recall@10
heron-fp16   zh    0.412     0.724     0.802
heron-int6   zh    0.405     0.710     0.756  <-- delta -0.046 at R@10
heron-fp16   en    0.448     0.768     0.829
heron-int6   en    0.446     0.761     0.824  (small)
heron-fp16   es    0.439     0.752     0.810
heron-int6   es    0.435     0.748     0.805
```

ada: that's a pretty localized drop in zh at R@10. R@1/5 less affected. could be cluster aliasing or tokenization differences after quant. did you run whiten/normalize the same?
jia: yes same pipeline: L2 norm + PCA whitening (trained on en+es). important detail: whitening transform was learned on en+es only, not zh.
ryan: aha. that could explain language shift interacting with quant noise. whitening transform not representative of zh manifold -> quantization noise pushes points across cluster boundaries at larger k.
matt: can we try whitening trained with zh included? quick A/B?
jia: started another run with zh included in whitening sample. kicked off at 6177779200, ETA ~9m.
eval-bot: run 6177779200 completed: heron-int6 zh recall@10 improved to 0.789 (vs 0.756). heron-fp16 zh unchanged. logs: /meta/bench/6177779200.log

jia: interesting, adding zh into whitening recovered ~70% of the gap. suggests representational shift + quant interaction.
ryan: good signal. still want to sanity-check embedding norm distributions pre/post quant. can you dump stats? mean L2 and stdev by lang + model.
jia: pasted stats:
```
metric        model      lang  mean_norm  std_norm
embedding_norm heron-fp16 zh    12.4       2.1
embedding_norm heron-int6 zh    11.9       3.8  <-- int6 has heavier tail
embedding_norm heron-fp16 en    12.6       2.0
embedding_norm heron-int6 en    12.5       2.2
```

ada: heavier tail on int6 zh supports the idea that some vectors get clipped/perturbed more. maybe per-channel quant calibration for zh tokens would help.
matt: can we try per-channel quant (per-channel scale) vs symmetric per-tensor? that's a short config change.
jia: queued two runs: per-tensor int6 (current) and per-channel int6. per-channel run id 6177780001.
eval-bot: run 6177780001 finished: heron-int6-perchannel zh recall@10 = 0.798, mean_norm=12.2 std=2.4.
ryan: per-channel almost matches fp16. nice. so root cause is quant granularity interacting with cross-lingual whitening + zh tail.
matt: next steps: update onboarding checklist to include language representation checks for whitening training, and prefer per-channel quant for multilingual models (unless cost delta unacceptable). also add a microbench case that reports recall@k per-lang and norm distribution.
ja: will open PR with: checklist changes, bench script flags, and a short note about whitening sampling.
ryan: also add a quick heuristic to fail int6 automated canaries if per-lang R@10 drops > 0.03 vs baseline.
ada: agree. and add a comment in model card describing that whitening dataset must cover intended languages.
matt: thanks all — good quick detective work :thumbsup:
